name: rumbledb
desc: JSONiq and XQuery query engine on Apache Spark
why: JSONiq and XQuery running on Spark is an unusual query language world, though heavy and niche.

brief.what_it_is: RumbleDB is an open-source query engine that runs JSONiq and XQuery on Apache Spark. You write a query in the JSONiq language and point it at nested or messy data such as JSON, JSON Lines, XML, CSV, Parquet, Avro, libSVM, or text, from a local disk, HDFS, S3, or Azure blob storage. Results come out as JSON, XML, CSV, Parquet, YAML, and other formats. It can run on a laptop or scale out across a Spark cluster, including Amazon EMR. The homepage calls version 3.0 'Coast Redwood'.
brief.why_it_exists: The README argues that RumbleDB exposes a query language rather than a DataFrame API, for more flexibility and productivity, and because a lot of data simply will not fit in DataFrames. The homepage pitches it as built for 'Big data. Nested data. Beautifully messy data.'
brief.how_it_works: Queries are written in JSONiq, a FLWOR-based language for nested data, and run on top of Apache Spark. The homepage says JSON navigation, FLWOR clauses, and downward XML navigation are automatically parallelized across cores or a cluster, and that count and sum-style pushdowns are applied automatically. The README does not describe the internals in more detail.

commands_seen.context: Listed on the homepage as the Python installation route ('Installation via pip install jsoniq'). Not shown as a separate code block.

brief.install_notes: The homepage lists installation via pip (the jsoniq package), Homebrew, Docker, a standalone jar, and a thin jar for use with an existing Spark installation, plus a Java API and an interactive query shell. There is a Jupyter notebook integration, and the README points to a Colab sandbox notebook (RumbleSandbox.ipynb) that can also be run locally. Running on a cluster needs Spark; the homepage says it runs on Amazon EMR (8.x) with data on S3 or HDFS. The homepage says Spark 4.0, 4.1, and 4.2 are supported. PostgreSQL and MongoDB reading is listed as Python-edition only. I saw no account or registration step; the homepage says none is needed.
brief.standout: It is a declarative nested-data query language sitting on Spark rather than a DataFrame API, and it accepts both JSONiq and W3C XQuery. The homepage claims 95% W3C compliance. It also bundles RumbleML, which exposes Spark ML estimators and transformers as JSONiq function items, so model training runs inside the query language.
brief.status: Appears maintained, but I could not confirm dates. The homepage advertises a current 3.0 release with Spark 4.2 compatibility, and the README points to docs for 'the latest official release'. I saw no release date or last-commit date in either page, so this is an inference from the version and compatibility claims.
brief.caveats: The engine is heavy: it runs on Spark, so you need a JVM and Spark for anything beyond a small local query. Some features are Python-edition only (PostgreSQL and MongoDB reading). The homepage's 95% W3C compliance figure is self-reported. The README says the Jupyter introduction to the RumbleDB-specific input formats has not yet been converted to notebooks. The homepage describes the project as niche. The README does not give a licence beyond the homepage's 'Apache 2.0' statement, and the brew formula notes were empty.
quotes: Big data. Nested data. Beautifully messy data.
RumbleDB exposes a query language rather than a DataFrame API, for more flexibility, more productivity but also because a lot of data simply will not fit in DataFrames.
You can query it in place from any local file systems or data lakes (Azure blob storage, Amazon S3, HDFS, etc).
